editor_notes.content_quality: Clean 658-word News brief on EndoQuest Robotics' PARADIGM pivotal trial enrollment completion. Standard Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis structure. Appropriately hedges every statistic as 'preliminary' and flags in 'What We Don't Know' that data verification and final statistical analysis are still pending — correctly frames this as a self-reported corporate milestone, not a peer-reviewed result.
editor_notes.source_verification: Manifest at sources/2026-07/endoquest-robotics-completes-enrollment-in-pivotal-trial-reports-100-en-bloc-resection-rate/manifest.json shows 2 sources: (1) aijourn.com — snapshot source-1.html.gz saved successfully, sha256 1345724110fc781f3915cc464f22cde679c35c22f7c8d3f275ab60dcf2815352 verified by decompressing and rehashing (matches manifest); read the full decompressed HTML. (2) medicaldevice-network.com — automated fetch returned HTTP 403 (bot-blocked), file: null, no archive.org fallback available in the manifest. Per the review skill's Step 3c fallback procedure, I WebFetched the live URL directly as a last resort, in two independent passes with different extraction prompts (one targeting stats/quotes, one targeting full verbatim quote text) to guard against summarization hallucination. Both passes returned identical, internally consistent text. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: this source is verified via live fetch only, not a locally committed snapshot -- unlike the aijourn.com source, no hash-verifiable archive of medicaldevice-network.com's content is preserved in this provenance record beyond my two WebFetch reads recorded here.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every stat in the article body traces verbatim to the medicaldevice-network.com content confirmed via WebFetch: 49 participants ('The multicentre investigational device exemption (IDE) study involved 49 participants'), 50 ESD procedures ('a total of 50 robotic endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) procedures'), 100% en bloc / 100% conversion-free ('Preliminary trial data showed a 100% en bloc resection rate and a 100% conversion-free rate'), 95.8% R0 ('the R0 resection rate was 95.8%'), no device-related bleeding/perforations, and both the Magnasco and Fonseca quotes reproduced word-for-word including the full second sentence of each ('We look forward to completing data verification...' / 'These preliminary results underscore...PARADIGM marks a major milestone...'). The Dec 2024 IDE-award date and the De Novo Classification Request sentence also match verbatim. The trial-site list -- 'AdventHealth in Orlando, Baylor St. Luke's in Houston, Cleveland Clinic in Cleveland, HCA Healthcare in Houston and Mayo Clinic in Scottsdale' -- matches the medicaldevice-network.com (July) content character-for-character in the same order. Separately, the aijourn.com snapshot (the January 15, 2026 BusinessWire press release reproduced by The AI Journal) lists a DIFFERENT site list: 'HCA Healthcare (Houston), Mayo Clinic (Scottsdale), Cleveland Clinic (Cleveland), Brigham and Women's Hospital (Boston), and AdventHealth (Orlando)' -- i.e. Brigham and Women's Hospital instead of Baylor St. Luke's, and 50 subjects instead of 49. The submission's body_markdown attributes the site list ONLY to Medical Device Network (the July, final-enrollment source) and never cites the January site list -- confirming the bot's stated resolution of the January/July discrepancy was correctly implemented in the final article. The article does not surface the discrepancy itself (a minor completeness gap, not an accuracy defect, since the article never uses the stale list), and the January-sourced claims used in the article (FDA's January 2026 approval of the final enrollment stage following an interim safety review, and the 'investigational device...not yet available for commercial sale' disclaimer) both check out verbatim against the aijourn.com snapshot.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral throughout. Company quotes are clearly attributed as company statements, not adopted as the article's own voice. No promotional language beyond what is contained in direct quotes.

editor_notes.source_count_assessment: Only 2 sources for a News-category article is thin, so I gave this specific scrutiny per the review instructions. The headline/summary/lead claim (enrollment completion, 100% en bloc resection rate) is attributed exclusively to Medical Device Network, an established medtech trade publication already on config/source_allowlist.txt -- not a random or promotional outlet. The second source (The AI Journal) is used only for secondary/background claims (the January FDA approval milestone and the standard investigational-device disclaimer) and is itself a verbatim reproduction of a BusinessWire corporate press release, i.e. primary-source material, not editorial spin. The bot's PR description states that BusinessWire, MassDevice, MPO-Mag, and 01net.it were found during research but excluded because they were unreachable/403'd -- this submission's own source manifest only ever lists the 2 URLs that made it into article.sources (chief:review does not re-fetch URLs the bot chose not to cite), so this specific claim about excluded outlets cannot be independently confirmed from provenance artifacts alone. However, the bot's stated practice (declining to cite outlets it could not itself verify) is the correct and conservative behavior, and is consistent with what I independently found: the two URLs actually cited are both real, both fully verified against their content, and adequately support every claim in the article. I consider sourcing adequate for a corporate-trial-milestone News brief given this verification, notwithstanding the low count.
concerns: medicaldevice-network.com (the source underlying nearly every specific statistic and both direct quotes) returned HTTP 403 to the automated snapshot fetcher and has no committed local snapshot or archive.org fallback in this provenance record -- verification rests on two independent live WebFetch reads performed during this review rather than a hash-verifiable archived file, unlike the aijourn.com source.

aijourn.com is not yet on config/source_allowlist.txt; it is a legitimate industry-press outlet (part of the Tiny Media Brands network) reproducing a BusinessWire release verbatim, but this is worth a maintainer follow-up to add it if it recurs as a source.

If medicaldevice-network.com continues to bot-block the automated fetcher across future submissions, consider adding it to an archive.org-first fetch strategy so future provenance records have a durable committed snapshot rather than relying on reviewer-time WebFetch verification.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Both automated warnings (allowlist gap, bot-blocked source) are sourcing-infrastructure issues, not content-accuracy defects. I independently verified every statistic, both direct quotes, the trial-site list, and the resolution of the January-vs-July site-list discrepancy against the actual source content (one via a hash-verified local snapshot, one via live WebFetch fallback after the automated snapshot fetch was bot-blocked). Nothing in the published article is inaccurate, so no corrections record is warranted -- this overrides the script's mechanical APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS default per the reviewer note in scripts/chief_editor_review.ts ('the human chief editor's editor_notes always has final say').
